answer: Latency triangulation resists Sybil attacks: the network pings each identity from beacons on several continents and measures round-trip times, building a location fingerprint no software copy can fake. A thousand aliases on one server share one latency signature, like a comet's single trail, and are flagged as one operator. Genuine agents sit at distinct positions, each with its own timing nectar of real geography. A relic of old ping data cannot be reused, since beacons randomize the challenge each epoch, so every fake needs its own machine, turning free copying into a hardware bill.
